items.title: Tony Awards Extends CBS Broadcast Agreement Through 2032
items.summary:
The Tony Awards will stay on CBS through 2032. The network, the American Theatre Wing and The Broadway League announced the extended broadcast agreement, continuing a relationship that began when CBS first carried the Broadway ceremony in 1978 and has now run 48 years.

The next milestone under the deal is the 80th Annual Tony Awards, set for Sunday, June 13, 2027. CBS will air the ceremony live to both coasts, with a simultaneous stream on Paramount+ Premium in the United States. Deadline reported the renewal, noting that further details on the 2027 show will follow in the coming weeks.

Heather Hitchens, president and CEO of the American Theatre Wing, and Jason Laks, president of The Broadway League, framed the extension around the approaching anniversary in a joint statement. "For the past 48 years, we have collaborated with CBS to bring the best of Broadway to theatre fans all around the world and we look forward to marking the 80th anniversary of the Tony Awards with our best show yet," they said.

Amy Reisenbach, president of CBS Entertainment, tied the renewal to the network's broader record on arts programming. "CBS has a celebrated history of supporting the creative arts on television and the Tony Awards are a cornerstone of that past, present and future," she said, crediting George Cheeks alongside her in extending the partnership.

The production team carries over. Raj Kapoor, Sarah Levine Hall and Jack Sussman return as producers on the 2027 telecast, with Kapoor and Levine Hall serving as co-showrunners. Patrick Menton and Rob Paine will co-executive produce, and Menton also takes on head of talent duties. The ceremony is produced in collaboration with Tony Award Productions, the joint venture between the American Theatre Wing and The Broadway League.

With the agreement running to 2032, CBS has locked in the Tonys past the 80th edition and through several more cycles, keeping the only major awards show devoted to Broadway on broadcast television for at least another six years.

items.title: Bob Dylan, Wearing Hoodie, Meets Pope
items.summary:
Pope Leo XIV received Bob Dylan in a private audience at the Vatican on the morning of November 4. The Vatican's Dicastery for Communication published photographs of the meeting, one of which shows Dylan in a black hoodie with the hood pulled up, apparently propped by a black baseball cap underneath.

A second image appears to show Dylan signing a book for the pope, having pulled off one glove to do it. Pitchfork noted the audience follows Leo's July meeting with Patti Smith, giving the pontiff two downtown New York icons in the space of a few months.

Dylan's relationship with Christianity has been long and uneven. Raised Jewish, he converted to evangelical Christianity in 1978 and released a run of Christian albums while working religious material into his live sets, to the bafflement of much of his audience. He scaled that back in later years, and in 1997 performed at a concert honoring Pope John Paul II.

Leo, for his part, has read deeper into the catalog than most. In the preface to Unarmed and Disarming: Peace Is a Gift, an anthology of his speeches, he quoted "Go Away You Bomb," a Dylan lyric written in 1963 for an unpublished collection of anti-nuclear poetry and little known outside of Dylan scholarship.

items.title: Cynthia Erivo to Play Tupac Shakur’s Mother in Universal’s Snoop Dogg Biopic (Exclusive)
items.summary:
Cynthia Erivo has joined the cast of Snoop, Universal Pictures' biopic of Snoop Dogg, in the role of Afeni Shakur, the mother of Tupac Shakur. The Hollywood Reporter reported the casting, with the film currently shooting in southern California.

Afeni Shakur was a former Black Panther activist whose difficult relationship with her son produced one of his defining records, the top 10 hit "Dear Mama." Camron Jones, who appeared in Amazon Prime's young adult drama Panic, plays Tupac. Jonathan Daviss of Netflix's Outer Banks takes the lead as Snoop Dogg, tracing the Long Beach rapper's rise through the 1990s.

The ensemble also includes Myles Bullock Be, Lauren London, Algee Smith, Tre Hale, Laya DeLeon Hayes, Olly Sholotan, Corey Champagne, Jonica Booth and SwayvoTwain. Craig Brewer is directing, with Imagine Entertainment's Brian Grazer producing alongside the company's Allan Mandelbaum. Snoop Dogg and Death Row Pictures president Sara Ramaker are also producing. Grazer previously produced 8 Mile, the semi-autobiographical Eminem drama.

Brewer, who recently made Song Sung Blue for Focus Features, wrote the most recent draft of the screenplay. Joe Robert Cole wrote the initial version. The film will draw on Snoop Dogg's catalog throughout.

Erivo has worked with Universal before, playing Elphaba in the studio's two-part Wicked adaptation, a performance that brought Golden Globe, SAG, Critics' Choice, NAACP, BAFTA and Academy Award nominations. She next appears in the film version of the stage play Prima Facie, which she executive produced through her Edith's Daughter banner and which premiered at the 2026 Toronto International Film Festival ahead of a November 13 release in UK and Ireland cinemas.

She also stars in Paramount's Children of Blood and Bone, opening January 15, 2027, opposite an ensemble that includes Viola Davis, Chiwetel Ejiofor, Idris Elba, Amandla Stenberg, Damson Idris, Regina King and Lashana Lynch. Erivo is represented by UTA, Entertainment 360 and Peikoff Mahan.
